reply: The A-coefficient b(t) decays from about 0.17 at early times to about 0.07 by t = 10, and it is well described by a slow decay with time constant near 0.06 (or 1/(1+0.035t)). Forcing the two time-dependences to share one rate constant raised the NMSE to 1.5e-2, so they run on different time scales.
